title: Ingress surge buffer & adaptive throttler for embeddings endpoint
creator: Lydia Chen
description: Goal: Reduce p99 latency spikes and avoid large overprovisioning for the embeddings/reranking route during tenant bursts. Deliver a combined lightweight ingress surge buffer + adaptive throttler that smooths short-lived bursts, applies tenant-aware admission control, and cooperates with the existing autoscaler and rate-limiter. Targets: p95 < 30ms, p99 < 150ms for single-request embeddings under normal load; tail amplification during 10s bursts should not exceed 2x baseline. Cost overhead budget: <= 12% in steady-state. Success criteria: (1) p99 improvement measured on canary traffic and synthetic burst tests, (2) autoscaler activity reduced for microbursts (fewer scale-ups on <60s spikes), (3) no increased error rate or CPU OOMs, (4) rollout plan with easy rollback to current admission behavior.
design_summary: We will place a small, memory-bounded FIFO surge buffer at the ingress of embeddings workers. Requests hitting the buffer are prefetched into a lightweight admission queue that exposes per-tenant slots and token-based fairness weights. The adaptive throttler observes 3 signals: worker queue depth, recent p99 latency, and autoscaler provisioned count. If signals indicate sustained pressure, we move from buffering to gradual shedding with token-based leases (short TTL) and informative 429s with 'Retry-After' and an optional client-backoff hint. The buffer favors short jobs (embedding-only) over long re-rank batches to preserve latency SLOs. Trade-offs: buffering reduces immediate rejects but increases latency for enqueued requests; shedding preserves latency for passing requests but increases errors. We will expose config knobs per customer tier (free/paid/enterprise) in the Console and default to conservative enterprise headroom. Integrations: hooks for Console metrics, Redis for buffer persistence during leader failover, and a compat layer for Private deployments that prefer local in-memory buffers.
implementation_plan: Add admission queue + per-tenant weight in runtime (opt-in flag runtime.ingressBuffer.enabled)
Expose tunables in Console: buffer_size, short_job_threshold_ms, tenant_weight_map
Add autoscaler observer: feed ingress signals to predictive autoscaler and create a temporary headroom budget
Run canary on 5% of embedding traffic for two weeks with detailed tracing
Full rollout with gradual percentage increase and automated rollback if p99 regressions > 10%
benchmarks_and_results: Synthetic burst test (100 tenants, 60s spike): baseline p99=420ms, prototype p99=130ms, steady-state cost +7%
Tail injection test (single hot-tenant): queue-depth-based admission reduced average scale-ups by 42% over 24h
Rerank-heavy traffic: small impact on embedding-only latency when prioritization enabled; end-to-end RL rerank latency unchanged within error margin
updates: 2026-02-25: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime and Autoscale owners. Agreed to use a bounded FIFO in front of worker pools and to keep buffer residency < 1s for typical bursts.
2026-03-01: Prototype implemented; initial microbenchmarks look promising. Observed increased memory churn on older worker images — tracked as ENG-256842.
2026-03-04: Design review with PMs and Product — approved tenant-weighted fairness; need explicit admin controls for enterprise customers.

2026-03-08: Canary rollout to 5% traffic started. Early telemetry indicates p99 reduction on synthetic bursts and no increase in 500s. Monitoring alerts added for buffer saturation and unexpected swaps.
2026-03-10: Blocker discovered: in Private/on-prem builds with strict memory caps, buffer persistence to Redis causes higher latency. Implementing an in-memory fallback and per-deployment config.
Next: finish in-memory fallback, extend e2e tests, prepare Console feature flag and rollout runbook.
comments: Aisha Kapoor (PM): Please ensure the Console exposes an 'emergency-shed' toggle and clear messaging for 429s so customers know their clients need backoff.
Marcus Alvarez (SRE): Add runbook steps for diagnosing buffer starvation and a playbook for temporarily widening headroom if we see oscillation.
Nina Park (Design): UI copy for Retry-After must be actionable. Drafted copy in the Console mock linked above.
Diego Morales (Assignee): Noted — will add emergency toggle and extend 429 payload with structured 'backoff_hint' field.
notes_for_oncall: If buffer saturation crosses 80% for >5min, oncall should: (1) enable emergency-shed for offending tenant(s), (2) increase autoscaler headroom temporarily, (3) check for long-running rerank jobs tying up resources. Dashboards: embeddings/ingress/buffer-utilization and autoscaler/scale-events.
rollout_runbook: Stage 1: feature flag disabled by default; enable for testorg and run synthetic burst tests
Stage 2: enable for 5% production traffic, monitor p99/5xx/errors for 48h
Stage 3: 25% traffic for 72h; validate Autoscaler activity and cost delta
Stage 4: 100% rollout with monitoring and 30-day observation window
Rollback criteria: sustained p99 regression > 10% or 5xx increase > 0.5% over baseline
